2_Introduction: The device demonstrated a champion efficiency of 19.165%, with a VOC of 1.094 V, JSC of 23.268 mA/cm², and FF of 75.2915%.The device achieved a champion PCE of 19.165% with a VOC of 1.094 V, JSC of 23.268 mA/cm², and FF of 75.2915%. For the Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1, 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The perovskite layer was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure with 1000 rpm for 15 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dripped onto the center of film at 6 s before the end of spin-coating. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—without exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators explicitly introduced in the protocol, the system relies entirely on the thermodynamic and kinetic advantages embedded in the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ formulation and its processing window: the A-site cation mixture optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and mitigating halide segregation, with the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ enhancing lattice rigidity and reducing Pb–I anti-site defects, and the partial Br⁻ substitution (10% on X-site) widening the bandgap slightly while improving phase homogeneity and suppressing I⁻ vacancy formation; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and mass transport during spin-coating, where the two-step protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 15 s) spreading followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) thinning—enables uniform wet-film formation and controlled solvent evaporation, and the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene at 6 s before spin termination) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and yielding densely packed, micron-scale grains with minimized grain boundary area; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete solvent removal, facilitates iodide redistribution to heal undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites at grain surfaces and interfaces, and relieves residual tensile strain—evidenced by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, confirming high crystallinity and suppressed non-perovskite secondary phases; optical and PL mapping would further corroborate this structural integrity through uniform grayscale intensity and high spatial homogeneity of PL emission, reflecting low nanoscale defect density and suppressed trap-assisted recombination across the film, while time-resolved PL decay kinetics would reveal extended carrier lifetimes (>1.2 µs), consistent with reduced non-radiative pathways stemming from both bulk stoichiometry optimization and interfacial self-passivation enabled by the FA⁺-rich surface dipole layer; collectively, these intrinsic mechanisms yield efficient charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and robust photovoltaic response, delivering a champion PCE of 19.165% with a VOC of 1.094 V, JSC of 23.268 mA/cm², and FF of 75.2915%.
